The '''2022 Hounslow London Borough Council election''' took place on 5 May 2022. All 62 members of [[Hounslow London Borough Council]] were elected. The elections took place alongside [[2022 London local elections|local elections in the other London boroughs]] and [[2022 United Kingdom local elections|elections to local authorities across the United Kingdom]].

In the [[2018 Hounslow London Borough Council election|previous election in 2018]], the [[Labour Party (UK)|Labour Party]] maintained its control of the council, winning 51 out of the 60 seats with the [[Conservative Party (UK)|Conservative Party]] forming the council opposition with the remaining nine seats. The 2022 election took place under new election boundaries, which increased the number of councillors to 62.

== Background ==

=== History ===
The thirty-two [[London boroughs]] were established in 1965 by the [[London Government Act 1963]]. They are the principal authorities in Greater London and have responsibilities including education, housing, planning, highways, social services, libraries, recreation, waste, environmental health and revenue collection. Some of the powers are shared with the [[Greater London Authority]], which also manages passenger transport, police and fire.<ref>{{Cite web|title=The essential guide to London local government {{!}} London Councils|url=https://www.londoncouncils.gov.uk/who-runs-london/essential-guide-london-local-government|access-date=2021-10-10|website=www.londoncouncils.gov.uk}}</ref>

Since its formation, Hounslow has generally been under [[Labour Party (UK)|Labour]] control, apart from a period from 1968–1971 when the [[Conservative Party (UK)|Conservative Party]] held a majority of the seats and a period from 2006–2010 when [[no overall control|no party had an overall majority]] of seats. Labour regained control of the council in the [[2010 Hounslow London Borough Council election|2010 election]], when they won 35 seats with 35.2% of the vote and the Conservatives won 25 seats with 32.0% of the vote. No Liberal Democrats, independents and residents' group councillors were elected in 2010, 2014 or 2018. In the [[2018 Hounslow London Borough Council election]], Labour extended its majority to win 51 seats with 54.1% of the vote, while the Conservatives won the remaining 9 seats, all in [[Chiswick]], with 28.8% of the vote across the borough. The Liberal Democrats won 8.1% of the vote and the Green Party won 7.8% of the vote, but neither party won any seats.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Holder|first=Josh|title=Local council elections 2018 – results in full|url=http://www.theguardian.com/politics/ng-interactive/2018/may/04/local-council-election-results-2018-in-full|access-date=2021-10-10|website=the Guardian|date=4 May 2018 |language=en}}</ref>

=== Council term ===

A Labour councillor for Heston West, Rajinder Bath, died in June 2019. He had been first elected in 1990 and had served as mayor in 1998.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Hounslow|first=London Borough of|title=Cllr Rajinder Bath - Heston West Ward|url=https://www.hounslow.gov.uk/news/article/775/cllr_rajinder_bath_-_heston_west_ward|access-date=2021-10-19|website=www.hounslow.gov.uk|language=en}}</ref> The former council leader and sitting Labour councillor for the Feltham North ward, John Chatt, died in August 2019. He had served as a councillor for twenty-nine years.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Cann|first=Ged|date=2019-08-30|title=Tributes paid after death of one of Hounslow's longest serving councillors|url=https://www.mylondon.news/news/west-london-news/tributes-one-hounslows-longest-serving-16842169|access-date=2021-10-19|website=MyLondon|language=en}}</ref> By-elections to fill both seats were held on 12 December 2019 to coincide with the [[2019 United Kingdom general election|2019 general election]]. Bath's seat of Heston West was won by the Labour candidate Balraj Sarai, while the Conservative Party candidate Kuldeep Tak gained Chatt's seat in Feltham North.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Hounslow|first=London Borough of|title=Election results|url=https://www.hounslow.gov.uk/info/20043/elections_and_voting/1177/election_results|access-date=2021-10-19|website=www.hounslow.gov.uk|language=en}}</ref> A Labour councillor for Hounslow Heath, Hina Kiani, resigned in July 2020 for work reasons.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Hossein-Pour|first=Anahita|date=2021-04-16|title=The candidates vying to be Hounslow councillors in May by-elections|url=https://www.mylondon.news/news/west-london-news/candidates-vying-hounslow-councillors-elections-20396091|access-date=2021-10-19|website=MyLondon|language=en}}</ref> The Labour councillor for Cranford ward, Poonam Dhillon died in January 2021. She had represented the ward since 2006–2014 and was re-elected in 2018.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Tributes paid to Cllr Poonam Dhillon|url=https://hounslowherald.com/tributes-paid-to-cllr-poonam-dhillon-p11936-95.htm|access-date=2021-10-19|website=hounslowherald.com}}</ref> Due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic]], by-elections for both seats were delayed until 6 May 2021, alongside the [[2021 London mayoral election]] and the [[2021 London Assembly election|London Assembly election]]. Hounslow Heath was held for Labour by Madeeha Asim, while Cranford ward was held for Labour by Devina Ram, with the Conservatives coming in second place in both wards.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2021-05-08|title=London Elections 2021 Day Two: By-election round-up|url=https://www.swlondoner.co.uk/news/08052021-london-elections-2021-day-2-by-election-round-up/|access-date=2021-10-19|website=South West Londoner|language=en-GB}}</ref>

As with most London boroughs, Hounslow elected its councillors under new boundaries decided by the [[Local Government Boundary Commission for England]], which it produced after a period of consultation. The number of councillors rose to 62, an increase from the previous 60, across eighteen three-councillor wards and four two-councillor wards.<ref>{{Cite web|title=LGBCE {{!}} Hounslow {{!}} LGBCE Site|url=http://www.lgbce.org.uk/all-reviews/greater-london/greater-london/hounslow|access-date=2021-10-19|website=www.lgbce.org.uk|language=en}}</ref>

== Campaign ==
Darius Nasimi, who came to the United Kingdom as an [[Afghanistan|Afghan]] refugee in 1999, was selected as a Conservative candidate for Hanworth.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2021-12-20|title=Afghan refugee who arrived in Britain in a lorry runs for Hounslow council|url=https://www.swlondoner.co.uk/news/20122021-afghan-refugee-who-arrived-in-britain-in-a-lorry-runs-for-hounslow-council/|access-date=2022-02-15|website=South West Londoner|language=en-GB}}</ref> The Labour councillor Theo Dennison resigned from his party after his motion of no confidence in council leader Steve Curran failed.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-03-07 |title=Hounslow Council's controversial leader to stand down due to ill health |url=https://www.swlondoner.co.uk/news/07032022-hounslow-council-controversial-leader-to-stand-down |access-date=2022-03-23 |website=South West Londoner |language=en-GB}}</ref> Curran later announced he would not be seeking re-election due to illness.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2022-03-01|title=Council Leader Stuns Meeting By Announcing Departure|url=http://www.brentfordtw8.com/default.asp?section=community&link=http://neighbournet.com/server/common/hounspol205.htm|access-date=2022-03-04|website=BrentfordTW8|language=en-GB}}</ref>

== Electoral process ==
Hounslow, like other London borough councils, elects all of its councillors at once every four years. The previous election took place in 2018. The election took place by multi-member [[first-past-the-post voting]], with each ward being represented by two or three councillors. Electors had as many votes as there are councillors to be elected in their ward, with the top two or three being elected.

All [[Elections in the United Kingdom#Registration procedure|registered electors]] ([[British citizen|British]], [[Irish citizen|Irish]], [[Commonwealth citizen|Commonwealth]] and [[European Union]] citizens) living in London aged 18 or over were entitled to vote in the election. People who lived at two addresses in different councils, such as university students with different term-time and holiday addresses, were entitled to be registered for and vote in elections in both local authorities.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|title=How the elections work {{!}} London Councils|url=https://www.londoncouncils.gov.uk/who-runs-london/london-elections/how-elections-work|access-date=2021-09-14|website=www.londoncouncils.gov.uk}}</ref> Voting in-person at polling stations took place from 7:00 to 22:00 on election day, and voters were able to apply for postal votes or proxy votes in advance of the election.<ref name=":1" />

* Heston Central Councillor Harleen Atwal resigned from the Labour Party to sit as an Independent in November 2025.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Lynch |first1=PJ |title= 'It's toxic': 2 more West London councillors resign from Labour ahead of 2026 local elections|url= https://www.mylondon.news/news/west-london-news/labour-party-resignations-london-elections-32847571.amp |access-date=25 Nov 2025 |work=MyLondon |date=10 Nov 2025}}</ref>
* Heston Central Councillor Riaz Gull resigned from the Labour Party to sit as an Independent in November 2025.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Lynch |first1=PJ |title= 'It's toxic': 2 more West London councillors resign from Labour ahead of 2026 local elections|url= https://www.mylondon.news/news/west-london-news/labour-party-resignations-london-elections-32847571.amp |access-date=25 Nov 2025 |work=MyLondon |date=10 Nov 2025}}</ref>
* Chiswick Gunnersbury Councillor Ranjit Gill, elected as a Conservative, joined Labour in May 2025.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Osborne |first1=Bridget |title=Chiswick councillor Amy Croft confirmed as Mayor of Hounslow for 2025–26 |url=https://chiswickcalendar.co.uk/chiswick-councillor-amy-croft-confirmed-as-mayor-of-hounslow-for-2025-26/ |access-date=31 May 2025 |work=Chiswick Calendar |date=27 May 2025}}</ref>
